numbered_results.label: thm:main
numbered_results.section_title: The main theorem and its context
numbered_results.title: Deterministic diagonal spectral separation
numbered_results.statement: For every n >= 2, Hermitian tridiagonal T with operator norm <= 1, and real 0 < delta < 1/2, return D = t diag(1,...,n), 0 <= t <= delta/n, with norm(D) <= delta and gap(T+D) > 2^(-88)(delta/n)^42 in O(n[1+log(n/delta)]^3) exact real operations and comparisons. Nonnegative square roots have unit cost; no input bits are extracted.
numbered_results.scope: The uniform matrix gap and exact-operation bound are proved in the paper. The cited certificate proves only the scalar and polynomial ingredients. It does not include Hermitian spectral theory, quasimodes, the gap implication, the value oracle or runtime. No finite-bit or floating-point conclusion follows from this cost model.

lean.name: KE02.coreCertificate
lean.scope: Aggregate of the scalar selector, Graeffe identities and coefficient inequalities, with precisely their stated hypotheses and exclusions.

numbered_results.label: lem:variational
numbered_results.title: Weighted spectral variational formula
numbered_results.statement: For every Hermitian A, f(A) = sum(j lambda_j(A)) is max tr(GA) over the unitary orbit of diag(1,...,n). Its operator-norm Lipschitz constant is W=n(n+1)/2; F(t)=f(T+tX) is convex with secant slopes in [W,nW].
numbered_results.scope: The spectral variational formula, Lipschitz inequality and matrix-specific convexity and slope bounds are not formalized. Lean takes scalar convexity and the initial potential bound as hypotheses.

numbered_results.label: rem:gauge
numbered_results.title: Reduction to real eigenvectors
numbered_results.statement: Diagonal unitary conjugation makes a Hermitian tridiagonal matrix real symmetric with nonnegative edges, separately on each connected component, and commutes with X and every real diagonal perturbation. The algorithm uses squared edge magnitudes without constructing the phases.
numbered_results.scope: The phase gauge and its spectral invariance are proved in the paper, including zero edges; there is no corresponding Lean declaration.

numbered_results.label: lem:quasimodes
numbered_results.title: Ordered disjoint-support quasimodes
numbered_results.statement: For real symmetric tridiagonal H of order n >= 2 and norm <= 2 with edges of magnitude <= 1, and orthonormal eigenvectors at eigenvalues differing by at most 0 < h <= 1/(256 n^6), put E=(lambda+mu)/2 and tau=(16 n^2 h)^(1/4). There are ordered disjoint-support unit vectors a,b with full-matrix residuals <= 2 n tau and b^T X b - a^T X a >= 1.
numbered_results.scope: The existence argument and its uniform quantifiers are paper proofs. Exact rational eigenpair and boundary fixtures check supporting identities and constants, not this all-matrix assertion.

numbered_results.label: lem:defect
numbered_results.section_title: Small gaps force a convexity defect
numbered_results.title: Small gaps force a convexity defect
numbered_results.statement: If H is real symmetric tridiagonal of order n >= 2 and norm <= 2, its edge magnitudes are <= 1, 0 < r <= 1, and gap(H) <= h_r = r^4/(10^12 n^14), then f(H+rX)+f(H-rX)-2f(H) >= r/2.
numbered_results.scope: The quasimode-to-defect implication, Hermitian flattening and weight-swap argument are proved in the paper. Rational examples and constant arithmetic supply finite supporting checks.

numbered_results.label: rem:repeated
numbered_results.section_title: Small gaps force a convexity defect
numbered_results.title: Repeated eigenvalues and the nearby matrix
numbered_results.statement: The small-gap proof includes gap(H)=0 by using the positive h_r and never dividing by the actual gap. The auxiliary Hermitian matrix H prime need not be tridiagonal.
numbered_results.scope: The degenerate spectral case and use of the auxiliary matrix are paper statements. Formal polynomial identities separately allow repeated roots, without proving this spectral remark.

numbered_results.label: lem:children
numbered_results.title: Child potentials and centered defect
numbered_results.statement: For a convex real function on [a,b] of positive length L, the middle-quarter children have potential sum at most the parent potential. At c=(a+b)/2 and r=L/4, the centered second difference is at most r times the parent potential.
numbered_results.scope: Both inequalities hold formally for every convex real function and every positive-length subinterval in its domain. The defect inequality is written in multiplied form, equivalent because r > 0. No spectral hypothesis is part of these declarations.

lean.name: KE02.selector_children_sum
lean.scope: The sum of the two actual middle-quarter child potentials is at most the parent potential.

lean.name: KE02.selector_defect_le
lean.scope: The centered second difference is at most selectorRadius times selectorPotential.

numbered_results.label: lem:robust-choice
numbered_results.title: Selection from approximate values
numbered_results.statement: If the four replies on each child of length ell have absolute errors <= ell/1024, choose the child with the smaller estimated potential, tying to the left. The next potential is <= parent potential/2 + 1/32; eight replies suffice.
numbered_results.scope: The arbitrary-interval potential error <= 1/64 is formalized. The recurrence, left tie rule and eight calls per round are proved for every round of the defined recursive selector under its reply contract. The paper states the one-step rule directly for an arbitrary interval. Replies are assumed; no value oracle is formalized.

lean.name: KE02.selector_estimate_error
lean.scope: For every positive-length interval and four replies within its tolerance, the estimated potential has absolute error <= 1/64.

lean.name: KE02.selector_potential_step
lean.scope: Potential recurrence along the defined scalar selector, for convex F and a valid reply stream.

lean.name: KE02.selector_choice_left
lean.scope: Actual approximate-reply estimates select the left child on equality.

lean.name: KE02.selector_choice_right
lean.scope: A strictly smaller right estimate selects the right child.

lean.name: KE02.selector_calls_count
lean.scope: The defined transcript has exactly 8j recorded calls after j rounds; this counts requests, not their evaluation cost.

numbered_results.label: prop:selector
numbered_results.title: Interval selection yields a separating tilt
numbered_results.statement: Start at [0,delta/n], take the least K with 2^K >= 16 n^3, and apply the approximate-value rule K times to F(t)=f(T+tX). The final midpoint c gives D=cX within budget and gap(T+D) > delta^4/(10^12 4096^4 n^42).
numbered_results.scope: The scalar conclusion through final potential < 1/8, defect < r/8, nested intervals, least K, radius > delta/(4096 n^7), left ties and exactly 8K calls is formal. The specialization to eigenvalues and conversion of defect into a matrix gap remain paper proofs. Convexity, initial potential and reply accuracy are explicit formal hypotheses.

lean.name: KE02.selectorCertificate
lean.scope: For every n >= 2, 0 < delta < 1/2, convex real F on [0,delta/n], initial potential < n^3, and reply stream meeting the absolute-error contract: the full finite scalar transcript, interval and radius bounds, and final defect < r/8. Spectral interpretation, reply construction and arithmetic cost are absent.

numbered_results.label: lem:multiply
numbered_results.section_title: Nearly linear evaluation in the exact arithmetic model
numbered_results.title: Polynomial multiplication in permitted operations
numbered_results.statement: For every m >= 0, polynomials of degree <= m can be multiplied in O((m+1)[1+log(m+1)]) permitted exact operations, with the needed algebraic constants constructed from rational numbers using nonnegative square roots.
numbered_results.scope: The radix-two Fourier construction, half-angle constants, convolution correctness and uniform operation count are proved in the paper. No FFT or operation-count theorem is formalized or established by the finite checks.

numbered_results.label: lem:spectral-approximation
numbered_results.section_title: Nearly linear evaluation in the exact arithmetic model
numbered_results.title: Gap-independent spectral approximation
numbered_results.statement: For every Hermitian tridiagonal A with norm <= 1 and 0 < epsilon < 1, compute nondecreasing approximations to every ordered eigenvalue with absolute error <= epsilon/2 in O(n[1+log(n/epsilon)]^2) permitted operations, without simplicity or gap assumptions.
numbered_results.scope: Lean proves the universal Graeffe and algebraic coefficient ingredients listed below. It does not prove the continuant-to-spectrum bridge, analytic ratio-root accuracy, sorting stability, spectral value oracle or operation count. The full spectral approximation lemma remains a paper proof.

lean.name: KE02.graeffeCertificate
lean.scope: Even/odd coefficient reconstruction for every real polynomial; Graeffe root squaring for every finite real root list, including empty lists, zero roots and repetitions, at every natural iteration count.

lean.name: KE02.coefficientCertificate
lean.scope: Coefficients of the actual product polynomial: expansion and leading coefficient; positivity, largest-product bounds and algebraic ratios for positive roots in decreasing order. The 2^k-th-root accuracy estimate is outside the statement.

numbered_results.label: thm:finite-bit
numbered_results.section_title: Finite-bit construction and a uniform enclosure certificate
numbered_results.title: Finite-bit diagonal regularization
numbered_results.statement: For n >= 2, d >= 2, delta=2^(-d), p and eta=2^(-p) as in Section 9.1, and a Hermitian tridiagonal proxy T0 on the eta grid enclosing each real input component within eta, a deterministic integer algorithm returns D=cX with 0 <= nc <= delta/4 and gap(T+D) > 2^(-100) delta^4/n^42 for every normalized T in that enclosure. Cost: O(n^2 p(1+log n)) operations on O(p)-bit integers, hence O(n^2 p^3(1+log n)) schoolbook bit operations; workspace and certificate size O(np), with p=O(log(n/delta)).
numbered_results.scope: The finite-information model, word-size, uniform gap and enclosure certificate theorems are proved in the paper. The constructor and independent rational verifier are tested on exact finite fixtures; these do not prove the uniform theorem or its cost. Verification may use longer integers; no bounded-word verification cost, nearly linear bit cost or floating-point stability theorem is asserted.

numbered_results.label: lem:bit-count
numbered_results.section_title: Finite-bit construction and a uniform enclosure certificate
numbered_results.title: Safeguarded integer inertia counts
numbered_results.statement: For grid tridiagonal A and grid query x, integer LDL pivots use signed floor division and replace zero pivots by -1. There is a real diagonal E with norm <= eta such that the negative pivot count equals the number of eigenvalues of A+E below x, and A+E-xI is nonsingular. Thus count >= j implies lambda_j(A) < x+eta; count < j implies lambda_j(A) > x-eta.
numbered_results.scope: The uniform diagonal-error interpretation and inertia implications are proved in the paper. The perturbation E may depend on x. The finite suite exercises signed division, zero replacement and exact rational inertia branches; there is no Lean formalization of these recurrences or spectral implications.

ingredients.title: Even/odd split and iterated root squaring
ingredients.statement: For P(z)=product(z+r_i), the actual transform E(-z)^2+z O(-z)^2 is product(z+r_i^2); after k transforms the roots are powered by 2^k.
ingredients.scope: Universal identities for real polynomials and every finite real root list, including the empty list, zeros and repeated roots. No positivity assumption or spectrum is used. Evaluation cost is outside the certificate.

lean.name: KE02.graeffeCertificate
lean.scope: Even/odd coefficient reconstruction for every real polynomial; Graeffe root squaring for every finite real root list, including empty lists, zero roots and repetitions, at every natural iteration count.

ingredients.title: Largest-product and algebraic ratio bounds
ingredients.statement: For positive roots in decreasing order, p_j <= e_j <= binomial(n,j) p_j <= 2^n p_j, and 2^(-n) r_j^(2^k) <= e_j/e_(j-1) <= 2^n r_j^(2^k). The ratio is the positive input to the root estimate.
ingredients.scope: The coefficients come from an actual product polynomial. The formal coefficient and ratio inequalities quantify over every valid n,k,j. The equation defining q_j is an anchor for its algebraic input only; extracting roots, bounding their analytic error and their cost remain in the paper.

lean.name: KE02.coefficientCertificate
lean.scope: Coefficients of the actual product polynomial: expansion and leading coefficient; positivity, largest-product bounds and algebraic ratios for positive roots in decreasing order. The 2^k-th-root accuracy estimate is outside the statement.

ingredients.title: Ratio roots and analytic spectral accuracy
ingredients.statement: Taking the 2^k-th root of the positive coefficient ratio gives r_j 2^(-n/2^k) <= q_j <= r_j 2^(n/2^k). For 1 <= r_j <= 3 and 2^k >= 6n/epsilon this yields absolute error <= epsilon/2.
ingredients.scope: The analytic root step and uniform accuracy are outside the Lean core. Rational outward root intervals verified by exact power comparisons check finite examples only. The eigenvalue identification and sorting argument are also paper proofs.

checks.scope: Exact integer and rational comparisons for the inverse-gap constant, potential error, recurrence, radius, exponent and evaluator allowance. These arithmetic identities do not prove the symbolic inequalities or runtime.
Finite continuant/determinant comparisons, positive-root families, Graeffe transforms, algebraic ratios and rational outward root intervals. Includes repeated roots and rejection controls.
Ninety rational convex piecewise-linear functions and 8,064 bounded-error replies; exact secants, derivative-integral comparisons, child choices, radius and centered defect. Finite fixtures only.

Nine rational eigenpair cases and separate rational fixtures for Wronskians, direction projectors, skipped rows, both truncation boundary entries, flattening, weight swaps and constants. These are supporting identities, not an all-input spectral proof.
Finite exact recursive polynomial and selector checks, including supplementary normalized characteristic identities that are not premises of the main construction.

Authenticated integer-constructor and independent rational-certificate suite, including fixtures of orders 2,3,4,8, exact norm/enclosure checks and malformed-data rejection. Normal, optimized and alternate hash-seed outputs must agree. The uniform guarantee and cost remain paper proofs.

Exact tests of safeguarded count branches, independent rational inertia, proxy enclosure, construction and certificate data, including complex and zero edges. No numerical eigenvalue routine is used for acceptance.
Reason-specific malformed-certificate, bracket, defect and input-mismatch rejection checks. Passing finite controls is not a proof of the universal finite-bit theorem.

scope: The exact-real and finite-bit theorems use different input and cost models. A unit-cost exact square root does not imply a bounded-bit implementation.
Nearly linear bit complexity for the full diagonal regularization problem remains open here. No stable floating-point implementation is proved.
The scalar Lean selector assumes valid approximate replies, convexity and an initial potential bound. Exactly 8K recorded requests do not certify the cost or existence of the spectral value oracle.

Hermitian spectral geometry, ordered-support quasimodes, small-gap-to-defect transfer, the continuant spectral interpretation, analytic ratio-root accuracy, sorting stability and both complete algorithmic cost arguments are proved in the paper only.

Finite certificates guarantee the conclusion conditionally for every normalized matrix in their specified enclosure. A passing certificate does not establish that the normalized part of the enclosure is nonempty.
The finite-bit construction has bounded word size. Its separate exact rational verifier may use longer integers; no bounded-word verifier complexity is claimed.

The map checks references and inventory. The separate Lean verification command compiles proofs and checks axioms; the mathematical verification entry point executes exact checks and rejection controls.
